clue.text: French nobleman getting into witness's bed

indicators.note: the nobleman is getting into the witness word, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to witness something is to see it
a duc is a French duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat climbs into the bed of someone who testified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like a noun at the end of the sentence, but it is the verb: to bed someone is to win them over sexually.
explanation.definitionFit: To bed someone is slang for winning them over and sleeping with them, which is to lead them astray.

clue.text: Use hands to make blind

indicators.note: the clue's letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to use their hands to make a window blind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' tells you to rearrange USE and HANDS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A window blind is a screen shutting out the glare of the sun.

clue.text: One succeeding another that's failed in service

definitions.text: One succeeding another that's failed in service

parts.words: One succeeding another that's failed in service
parts.note: in tennis a serve that fails a second time straight after a first failed serve loses the point

explanation.surface: Someone takes over from a colleague who failed in their job serving others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests employment, but it is the tennis serve: two failed serves in a row cost the point.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, two consecutive faulty serves make the server lose the point.

clue.text: Man of faith's preserve

definitions.meaning: a parish priest in France, a clergyman
to preserve meat or fish by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: A priest's jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A curé is a parish priest in France; separately, salting or smoking food keeps it from rotting.

clue.text: Lonely ladies to cut loose

indicators.note: letters cut loose from their order are free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lonely women are urged to break free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut loose' rearranges LADIES and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone isolated is cut off and solitary, hence lonely.

clue.text: It's Spooner's persuasive line of chat that makes yarn

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: winning, as in a winning smile, is persuasive
a spiel is a salesman's patter

explanation.surface: A smooth talker spins a yarn with persuasive chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of WINNING SPIEL gives SPINNING WHEEL. 'yarn' suggests a tall story, but it is wool thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning wheel is the household machine on which wool or flax is twisted into thread.

clue.text: Continue to wee at the death

parts.note: to last is to continue or go on
wee is Scottish for small, and minute means tiny

explanation.surface: Someone needs to keep going to the toilet right up to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like the verb for urinating, but it is the Scots word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: 'At the death' is sports slang for at the very end of a game, which is the final moment.

clue.text: Link with 9 on occasion?

definitions.meaning: a black ... event, black being the answer to 9, is a formal occasion

explanation.surface: Something connected with black on special occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie things is to fasten them together; and a black tie dinner is the formal dress code naming a bow worn at the neck.

clue.text: Daughters content to share piece of cake

indicators.note: the daughters are the content, held inside the other word

parts.note: a dole is a portion or share handed out
D is short for daughter, so two daughters are DD

explanation.surface: Two girls are happy to split a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy, but it means contained inside. 'piece of cake' is the idiom for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is British slang for something easy, a cinch.

clue.text: Extremes of writing not seen in the FT

definitions.text: Extremes of writing not seen in the FT

parts.words: Extremes of writing not seen in the FT
parts.note: printed text is normally dark ink on pale paper, but the Financial Times is printed on pink paper; the two colours are also opposite extremes

explanation.surface: Something about the far edges of the text that the newspaper never prints.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordinary newsprint is dark on pale, and 'in writing' is the idiom; the FT famously uses salmon-pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in writing, and names two opposite colours that a pink newspaper does not show together.

clue.text: 9 18 are about sensory fibres getting tense inside

indicators.note: the tense letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: neural means relating to nerves, the body's sensory fibres
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Something about nerve fibres in a tense state.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 18 is black and white, the colours with no hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Black and white carry no colour, so decorators call them neutral shades.

clue.text: Independent holds unsafe seat as a replacement

indicators.note: the independent word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: IND is the abbreviation for an Independent politician

indicators.note: an unsafe seat is wobbly, so its letters are unstable and shift

explanation.surface: An independent candidate keeps a marginal constituency in place of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsafe' is the anagram signal working on 'seat', and 'holds' puts the result inside; 'unsafe seat' sounds like an election marginal.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, as a substitute.

clue.text: A matter of some gravity after 9 's unbroken broadcast

definitions.text: A matter of some gravity after 9

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: whole means complete and unbroken

explanation.surface: A serious matter follows the black presenter's uninterrupted broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: After 9, black, this gives a black hole, a region of such strong gravity that no light escapes. 'gravity' seems to mean seriousness, but it is the physical force.
explanation.definitionFit: A black hole is a collapsed star whose gravitational pull is overwhelming.

clue.text: E number's outwardly ludicrous if not time-wasting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the ludicrous word sits outwardly, round the outside of the number

parts.note: comical means laughably ridiculous
NO is short for number

explanation.surface: A food additive's code is outwardly absurd unless it saves time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E number' looks like a food additive, but E stands alone; 'outwardly' says the ludicrous word wraps round the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means thrifty, using time or resources without waste.

clue.text: Actor in role developed interdependence

indicators.note: something developed is reworked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor grew into a part and came to depend on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges ACTOR, IN and ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A correlation is a mutual relationship where two things vary together, a kind of interdependence.

clue.text: Odin's son — nonsense!

parts.note: Balder is a Norse god, son of Odin
the printed mark is a dash

explanation.surface: An exclamation dismissing a remark about the Norse god's son.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark between the words is itself part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is a dismissive word for senseless talk, rubbish.

clue.text: Pay to get rid of loose ends?

definitions.meaning: to meet the cost of something

definitions.text: to get rid of loose ends?
definitions.meaning: reading the word as ..., to undo fraying, removing loose threads

explanation.surface: Settle up to tidy away unfinished business.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to settle them; whimsically, de-fraying would be removing frayed threads.

clue.text: Four points are in bag

parts.note: E, N, S and N are four compass points

explanation.surface: Four sharp items are inside a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to catch or trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag game is to capture it, just as one traps it in a net.

clue.text: See 9
Time when things looked 9?

parts.note: a period of history pictured as gloomy and black, when learning seemed to vanish

explanation.surface: A period when everything looked bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is black: the early medieval period is called dark because records and learning were scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: The early Middle Ages are traditionally pictured as a gloomy era of lost learning.

clue.text: Sweet, but not after 9

definitions.meaning: a dessert, called a sweet or pud in Britain
black, the answer to 9, placed before it gives a savoury blood sausage, which is no dessert

explanation.surface: A dessert, though not one eaten late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word means dessert, yet black pudding is a savoury sausage made with blood.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word is a general term for dessert, while black pudding is a savoury blood sausage.

clue.text: As glove on the other hand of goddesss

annotationWithheld.clue: As glove on the other hand of goddesss

clue.text: Fall asleep without removing hat?

parts.note: no means without, as in no money
to doff is to remove one's hat

explanation.surface: Someone drops off while still wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits differently from its meaning: no doff, not doffing one's cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to doze off involuntarily, drifting into sleep.

clue.text: See 5
Show rotgut can form excrescences

indicators.note: the letters can form something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cheap liquor can cause unsightly growths to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can form' rearranges SHOW and ROTGUT. Rotgut is cheap, harsh liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Excrescences are abnormal growths sprouting from a surface, like warts.

clue.text: This raises game after 9

definitions.meaning: a device for lifting a car
black, the answer to 9, followed by it gives a card game, also called twenty-one

explanation.surface: This increases the stakes in a game after nine o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A car jack is a lifting device; blackjack is the casino card game also called twenty-one.

clue.text: Area between 9 18?

parts.note: the shade midway between black and white, and an ambiguous zone that is neither one thing nor the other

explanation.surface: The space between black and white.
explanation.walkthrough: A grey area is an idiom for something not clearly right or wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey is the shade between black and white, and a grey area is an unclear zone.

clue.text: Process that brings art into the fold

definitions.text: Process that brings art into the fold

parts.words: Process that brings art into the fold
parts.note: a Japanese craft where creating artwork means folding sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A procedure that welcomes art into the community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into the fold' sounds like being accepted into a group, but here the art is literally made by folding paper.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese craft makes figures entirely by folding paper.

clue.text: Good opening's lost after 9's hazardous stuff

indicators.note: the opening letter is lost, so the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nice means good or pleasant

explanation.surface: A good opportunity is wasted after something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: After 9, black, this gives black ice, the invisible film on roads that makes driving dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Black ice is a thin transparent glaze on roads, notoriously treacherous for drivers.

clue.text: Faux pas to go without a dress accessory

indicators.note: one piece goes on the outside of the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: a faux pas is a social blunder, an erring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Committing a social blunder by going out without a fashion accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go without' seems to mean do without, but it means go round the outside of.
explanation.definitionFit: This piece of jewellery, worn on the lobe, completes an outfit.

clue.text: Newcomers' heartening refreshments

indicators.note: the word is the heart of the next word, buried inside it

explanation.surface: Encouraging snacks for new arrivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartening' looks like encouraging, but it says the answer lies in the heart of 'refreshments'.
explanation.definitionFit: First-year students at a college or university are its newcomers.

clue.text: Hollow cry reflectively intoned at site of suspected 9 12

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to intone is to chant, so sung

explanation.surface: A hollow cry echoes back from a place where something mysterious lurks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflectively' reads 'intoned' backwards. 9 12 is black hole: Cygnus X-1, in the Swan constellation, was the first strong black hole candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation of the Swan contains Cygnus X-1, the first object widely accepted as a black hole.
